query: For the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain why their mechanical properties differ during deformation and failure when constituent count alone is inadequate? Specify a controlled comparison, predictions relative to the quinary baseline, the applicable boundary conditions, supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Differences in mechanical properties among the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its subsets are due to variations in short-range order and local lattice distortions, which affect dislocation mobility and deformation mechanisms.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets in a single-phase FCC state after thermomechanical processing
generation.intervention: Controlled variation of alloy composition by removing one or more elements to create quaternary and ternary subsets
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order and local lattice distortions
generation.mechanism: Dislocation mobility and deformation mechanisms influenced by short-range order and local lattice distortions
generation.predicted_outcome: The quinary alloy will exhibit higher strength and lower ductility compared to its quaternary and ternary subsets, which will show varying degrees of strength and ductility based on their specific compositions
generation.boundary: Single-phase FCC microstructure, absence of precipitates or other secondary phases
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient data on the specific short-range order and local lattice distortions in each alloy subset, as well as potential interactions between these factors and other microstructural features

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of mechanical properties among the quinary alloy and its subsets using uniaxial tensile testing, with characterization of microstructure and short-range order using techniques such as X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the quinary alloy does not exhibit higher strength and lower ductility compared to its quaternary and ternary subsets, or if the variations in mechanical properties among the subsets do not correlate with differences in short-range order and local lattice distortions, the hypothesis isn't supported
